scope: Primary-source challenge to whether additional wafer, packaging, process-learning or software evidence justifies an incremental upside overlay. No frozen model, price target or pitch artifact was edited.
conclusion: The best new corroboration is MediaTek's direct description of a U.S. IDM packaging development program. It improves the credibility of the packaging opportunity already modeled. None of the reviewed disclosures establishes a separately identifiable incremental profit stream that can honestly be added to the current forecast without new assumptions about customer identity, fees, capital and overlap.

current_forecast_is_not_zero_option.working_capital_policy: 15% of net incremental revenue; no customer-funded float is assumed.
current_forecast_is_not_zero_option.host_warning: The original November4 packaging policy's host Foundry rows are stale. Current host values above were confirmed by the independent model reconstruction agent. Host aggregate Foundry recovery already includes existing external services; the model has not identified it as internal-only.
current_forecast_is_not_zero_option.interpretation: A $7B gross program forecast with a 25% operating margin and $5.5B additional physical capital through2030 is already a substantial commercial success assumption. Announcing a prospective packaging customer is not automatically upside to it. Neither MediaTek's entire ASIC revenue nor customer-consigned HBM/logic value belongs in Intel packaging revenue.

most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.source: MediaTek Q3 2026 earnings call transcript, October30
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.verified: Full text read; rendered pages7,8,11 visually inspected. Other passages checked in extracted text.
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.short_quote: we are working on this US IDM packaging process as our absolute priority
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.page7_to8: CEO describes active collaboration with the U.S. IDM and Japanese/Taiwanese substrate suppliers, identification of two or three important yield problems, and confidence in improvement. This is substantive engineering work, rather than a supplier merely claiming a large addressable market. The CEO does not disclose a yield percentage or establish completed qualification.
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.page7_schedule: Second-generation accelerator project remains targeted for high-volume manufacturing in Q12028; some dies have taped out while others follow on a slightly different schedule. The company says supply-chain details for2028 remain in process.
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.page8_to9_distinction: Separately, MediaTek confirms a second customer whose project is beginning and is expected to generate revenue in2028. This must not be confused with the second-generation accelerator project for its first customer. The packaging vendor for that second customer is not identified.
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.page11_identity_boundary: The analyst, not management, names Intel, EMIB-T and Google. The CEO responds that MediaTek is not dependent on one supplier and identifies TSMC as its most important partner. Intel is a plausible inference for the unnamed U.S. IDM, not a newly confirmed named Intel production contract.
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.financial_boundary: MediaTek's approximately$16B2027 accelerator revenue objective and $3.9B convertible funding do not disclose Intel packaging fees or a payment to Intel. Corporate operating-margin goals do not establish an Intel program margin.
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.bull: A buyer investing engineering resources in an alternative packaging architecture can create meaningful program-level switching costs and makes commercialization more credible.
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.bear: The same testimony confirms remaining yield work, supply-chain uncertainty and a deliberate multi-supplier strategy. A customer can value diversification while bargaining aggressively on price.
most_useful_new_buyer_evidence.model_action: Strengthen the evidence supporting the existing packaging scenario. Add no new revenue, profit, customer prepayment or named-customer assignment from this source.

competitive_packaging_check.fact: Intel describes silicon bridges embedded in organic substrates and EMIB-T's through-bridge power delivery. It presents large-package scaling and lower manufacturing cost as benefits.
competitive_packaging_check.boundary: The page supplies no matched product cost, qualified package yield, manufacturing throughput, realized price or customer margin. A technology feature is not a quantified economic advantage. The broad marketing assertion of exclusive heterogeneous integration is not adopted.

competitive_packaging_check.source: TSMC CoWoS technology page, accessed November5,2026
competitive_packaging_check.short_quote: RDL-based interposer, higher density embedded local silicon interconnect (LSI)
competitive_packaging_check.fact: CoWoS-L combines redistribution layers with local silicon interconnects and accommodates diverse embedded chips. TSMC says its initial3.5x-reticle CoWoS-L entered volume production in2024.
competitive_packaging_check.implication: Do not compare Intel's bridge approach exclusively with a large monolithic silicon interposer and imply that this describes all contemporary competing CoWoS. The actual comparison must include CoWoS-L's local bridges, power integrity, substrate yield, assembly yield and accepted output. No conclusion about equal cost or equal performance is possible from these descriptions.

competitive_packaging_check.fact: Management describes5x-reticle packaging in production and9x/14x work in development. It acknowledges competitive alternatives and stresses timely customer product launches when asked about supplying backup capacity. It also expects2026–28capital spending substantially above the prior three years.
competitive_packaging_check.boundary: The analyst asks explicitly about EMIB-T; the answer is not evidence that an Intel customer has switched or that TSMC has reserved a particular backup allocation. Reticle-size and roadmap claims are not matched qualification or cost comparisons.
competitive_packaging_check.local_download: HTTP403; read via web PDF extraction. No fake localPDF retained.

competitive_packaging_check.source: GlobalFoundries October8 announcement; November4Q3 presentation page8
competitive_packaging_check.fact: GF and TSMC announced a $2B manufacturing agreement for U.S. silicon interposers, with an initial five-year term and expected volume ramp in1H2028 at Malta,NewYork.
competitive_packaging_check.implication: Domestic advanced-packaging supply is also being developed by Intel's competitors and partners. U.S. location alone is not a defensible perpetual Intel-only margin moat.
competitive_packaging_check.boundary: This agreement is for interposer manufacturing, not the full package price; it does not by itself eliminate packaging shortages. Do not divide$2B by five to claim a uniform annual realized revenue schedule. The release does not assign all CoWoS-L requirements to GF.
competitive_packaging_check.verification: October8 HTML release read in full; it directly confirms$2B, initial five-year term and1H2028ramp. Q3deck search extraction corroborates but directPDFopen exceededwebsize limit and local downloadreturned403; no fullPDFreview claimed.

competitive_packaging_check.fact: Amkor reports customer commitments exceeding phase1's33,000square-meter planned cleanroom space; phase2adds60,000and raises total planned campus investment to$12B. Phase2construction is targeted for late2027throughend2029.
competitive_packaging_check.implication: The industry capacity response and customer commitments are real, but the factories need time and large capital outlays. This supports a capacity-cycle thesis, not guaranteed excess supply on an exact date.
competitive_packaging_check.boundary: Amkor is both an ecosystem partner and potential service competitor. Its site investment and broad OSAT operating margins cannot calibrate Intel EMIB-only capital turns or margins directly.

external_wafer_options.dated_evidence: Intel November2 describes PDK0.9as a design-start milestone and expectsPDK1.0inQ12027. Synopsys July27describes certified14Aflows, production-ready18A/18A-Pflows and EMIB/EMIB-T design integration.
external_wafer_options.bull: Design tools, silicon validation and interconnect planning lower customer integration risk and are necessary prerequisites for commercial wins.
external_wafer_options.boundary: Certification and design starts are not committed wafer volume, realized prices or qualified high-volume output. No additional revenue overlay is supported without a separately funded project assumption.

external_wafer_options.dated_evidence: Current technology material describes the2027collaboration. UMC's October28Q3report was checked; its additional$3.2Bboard-approved capacity plan concernsSingaporeandTainan, not a newly disclosed Intel12nm commitment.
external_wafer_options.bull: Reuse of installed mature manufacturing assets could be less capital intensive than a new leading-edge fab.
external_wafer_options.boundary: Customer awards, recognized revenue split, incremental cash outlay and profit sharing remain undisclosed. Do not assign UMC's unrelated capacity budget or total revenue to Intel.

external_wafer_options.dated_evidence: July21customer announcement corroborates a real Intel manufacturing/design/packaging relationship.
external_wafer_options.boundary: No disclosed large annual Intel fee, production ramp or project margin. Previously reviewed as evidence of actual commercialization, not a quantified incremental multibillion-dollar wafer stream.

external_wafer_options.assessment: AWS's mixed customXeon/fabric/coinvestment framework cannot all be counted as merchant wafer revenue and may overlap Products/OtherDCAI. An unnamed Microsoft18Adesign cannot be assigned to its announced TSMC-based Maia accelerator. Prior November4wafer adjudication remains controlling.

This is a break-even accounting exercise, not a wafer-yield forecast or an observed cost mix. See retained_profit_deepening.json.

This supports treating publicSPEC/Redisbenchmarks as initial screening rather than a production procurement decision. It discloses noIntelnetCPUpricing.

unit_share_recheck.conclusion: The20% own unit forecast is compatible with this primary industry forecast. unit_share_recheck.novelty: Rechecked prior work; not a new discovery.

what_would_change_the_valuation_evidence: A named buyer or Intel disclosure of an accepted commercial program, its launch date and minimum committed volume, followed by realized recurring revenue rather than one-time contract revenue.
Enough information to separate materials passed through, customer-consigned die/HBM, assembly fees and project operating costs, including yield losses and package-specificR&D.
Customer or partner funding terms tied to the same program, including repayment, discounts, capacity ownership and purchase obligations; prepayments alone are not profit.
A funded incremental capacity bridge that demonstrably sits outside the host Foundry and existing$7Bgrosspackaging scenario.

Evidence that subsequent premiumCPUprofit survives supplier-price negotiations, mix changes and competitor/customer alternatives, evaluated jointly with Foundry and capital rather thanDCAImargin alone.

pitch_recommendation: Use the buyer/supplier evidence to explain why a packaging ramp is credible and why it remains risky. The strongest defensible thesis is a conditional operating recovery with explicit purchase-price discipline, not an additional free-option narrative. More source count cannot resolve undisclosed net prices and program economics.
